text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.
Robusta futures in London ended higher following a firmer New York market. July closed $30 higher at $1,790 per tonne, while September gained $8 to close at $1,785 per tonne.

Arabica futures in New York closed higher across the board. Buying interest was fueled by a USDA attache report and forecasts of colder weather in Brazil although meteorologists seem to be in agreement that there is no risk of frost in the forecast. While yesterday's market was weighed down on the 'large' number of stocks pending grading, the fact that there is a high failure rate helped to ease these concerns. July closed 6.25 cents/lb higher at 191.50 cents/lb. September added 5.95 cents/lb to close at 171.65 cents/lb, while the deferreds closed 2.25 to 3.75 cents/lb higher.

BRAZIL - According to the US agricultural attache Brazilian coffee production in crop year 1997/98 (July/June) could reach 24 million bags, down from 27.5 million bags produced last year and 16.8 million bags produced in 1995/96. The report, prepared by an attache with the US embassy in Sao Paulo, said arabica production was forecast at 19.4 million bags, down from 22.3 million bags in 1996/97, while robusta production could reach 4.6 million bags, down from 5.2 million bags the previous year. The 1997/98 figure is down sharply from the USDA's official Brazil estimate of 28 million bags published in its 1997/98 world coffee production report in June. The release of the attache report also coincided with a revised 1997/98 estimate by Brazilian trade house Tristao which raised its forecast for the 1997/98 crop by 8.94 per cent to 25.6 million bags from an April forecast of 23.5 million bags. BRAZIL - Brazil's government is to auction 149,705 60-kg bags of coffee from its stocks at a regular monthly auction on July 8, the Banco do Brasil said. Members of the domestic roasting and soluble coffee industry as well as exporters can participate in the auction.

UNITED STATES - US certified coffee stocks rose by 2,893 60-kg bags as of July 7 to 55,369 bags, up from 52,476 bags on July 4 and 50,550 bags on July 3. 34,159 bags were pending grading. The exchange also reported that 8,152 bags were graded, but less than half (3,199 bags) had passed.

ITALY ** - Italy imported 477,441 bags of coffee in February 1997, 3.5 per cent less than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1997 up to 995,800 bags, 1.8 per cent less than was imported the same period in 1996. Total imports in calendar year 1996 rose by 4 per cent to 5.608 million bags. The dominant supplier of green coffee in January/February 1997 was Brazil with 279,700 bags, up from 248,200 bags supplied the same two months in 1996.

The country exported 125,500 bags of coffee in January/February 1997, nearly 3 per cent more than was exported the same period in 1996. Total exports in calendar year 1996 rose by 11 per cent to 822,500 bags.
